new_statements.rule_in_words: No statement about word stress anywhere in the pages for Martu Wangka / Manjiljarra / Kartujarra or the Western Desert introduction. The handbook is an annotated bibliography and language guide (location, names, classification, speaker numbers, spelling system, list of materials); it contains no phonological description, and for grammar it only points to Marsh (1976) The grammar of Mantjiltjara and Marsh (1969) 'Mantjiltjara phonology', Oceanic Linguistics 8(2):131-152.
new_statements.identity_note: Thieberger treats 'Martu Wangka' as the Jigalong communilect: 'Marsh (1972) says that Martu Wangka is the contemporary name for the language of Jigalong which is made up of Kartujarra, Putijarra and Manjiljarra' (sections 4.6.1 and 4.6.3), with over 700 speakers, nearly 400 of them Manjiljarra (Marsh 1990 p.c.). Marsh (1990 p.c.) describes it as 'a variant made up of two mutually intelligible languages, not mixed-up, but drawing synonyms and linguistic variations from more than one source' (section 4.6). No dialect-specific stress claims are made.
